Notepad++ and Don Ho: A story of software, activism, and defiance

For nearly 20 years, Notepad++ has been a staple in my workflow and one of the first programs I install on a new Windows computer.

The editor remains fast and dependable, while its open-source development model gives users confidence that the tool will remain available.

Its creator has also used release notes to speak about political events, connecting software maintenance with a broader defense of freedom.

Those messages have prompted readers to discuss both the program and the role developers can play in public life.
